_comment: strutil-core malicious RubyGems package reported by Socket on 2026-11-06, carrying a new build of the testmetest worm (Miasma family, derived from the public Shai-Hulud toolkit). The account jamnajiea published a clean 1.0.0 on 2026-11-01 and the malicious 1.0.1 under two hours later; 1.0.1 declares a native extension whose ext/strutil-core/extconf.rb downloads Bun 1.2.18 and runs the 5.48 MB ext/strutil-core/index.js at gem install time. The payload steals cloud, CI, registry, SSH, AI coding tool and wallet credentials, exfiltrates to paleasbest[.]top, self-propagates via RubyGems/npm/PyPI, installs persistence, poisons AI tool configuration, and includes a home-directory wiper triggered by token revocation. RubyGems removed both versions about five hours after the malicious release (rubygems.org now returns 404 for the gem). strutil-core 1.0.1 is corroborated by OSV MAL-2026-19054 (published 2026-11-01T20:00:00Z, finder Bitbison) and GHSA-gv9w-h836-5f8g (published 2026-11-10T00:32:04Z, references the OSV record). The related PyPI package pystr-codec 0.1.0, 0.1.1 and 0.1.2, which Socket ties to the same collection endpoint, is corroborated by OSV MAL-2026-18432 (published 2026-11-01T00:13:02Z, source kam193) and GHSA-f93h-mc69-274w (published 2026-11-01T03:30:23Z); PyPI returns 404 for all three versions. strutil-core 1.0.0 is omitted: Socket describes it as a clean seed release and neither OSV nor GHSA lists it as affected.
